subject: gk
question: Which scheme was rolled out to effectively integrate India’s manufacturing capabilities with the demands of global supply chains and to promote domestic value addition and exports?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Production Linked Incentive Scheme**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme was launched by the Government of India to boost manufacturing in the country.
 
• It aims to promote domestic manufacturing and reduce import dependence by providing incentives based on incremental sales from products manufactured in India.
 
• The scheme covers key sectors such as electronics, pharmaceuticals, automobiles, and textiles, among others.
 
• The PLI Scheme is designed to attract large-scale investments, enhance the competitiveness of Indian products, and integrate India into the global supply chain.
 
• As of 2023, the government has expanded the scheme to include more sectors and increase the financial outlay to further stimulate manufacturing growth in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Make in India Initiative**

 
 
• Launched in 2014, it aims to transform India into a global manufacturing hub by encouraging both multinational and domestic companies to manufacture their products in India.
 
• The initiative focuses on key sectors such as automobiles, chemicals, IT, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and more.
 
• It aims to increase the manufacturing sector's contribution to the GDP to 25% by 2025.
 
• Make in India promotes ease of doing business, innovation, skill development, and intellectual property rights.
 
 
 
• **Startup India**
 
 
• Launched in 2016, this initiative aims to build a strong ecosystem for nurturing innovation and startups in India.
 
• It focuses on simplifying regulatory frameworks, providing funding support, and fostering an entrepreneurial culture.
 
• Startup India offers various benefits including tax exemptions, patent filing support, and credit guarantee schemes.
 
 
 
• **Merchandise Exports from India Scheme (MEIS)**
 
 
• Introduced in 2015, MEIS aims to promote the export of notified goods manufactured in India.
 
• Under the scheme, exporters are rewarded with duty credit scrips which can be used to pay various duties and taxes.
 
• MEIS has been replaced by the Remission of Duties and Taxes on Export Products (RoDTEP) scheme from January 1, 2021.
 
 
 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat**
 
 
• Launched in 2020, it aims to make India self-reliant by promoting local products and reducing dependence on imports.
 
• It encompasses various measures including reforms in agriculture, MSMEs, and defense manufacturing.
 
• The initiative also focuses on boosting infrastructure, improving governance, and ensuring ease of doing business.
